title: The same note in many places
summary: One note can be played at more than one place on the fretboard.

steps.title: Two places for one note
steps.body:
The same note can often be played in more than one place. The open A string and fret 5 of the thickest E string are both A, and they sound the same.

**Why it matters:** When a song asks for a note, you can pick the place that is easiest to reach. Good guitarists choose the spot that keeps their hand close to the next note.

steps.title: Three places for one note
steps.body:
Some notes live in three places. D is at the open D string, at fret 5 of the A string and at fret 10 of the thickest E string. Each of these is a different string, but the pitch is the same.

**Why it matters:** Knowing the places helps you jump between strings without losing your way.

steps.title: Where can you find G?
steps.body: G is at the open G string. It is also at fret 5 of the D string and fret 10 of the A string.

items.prompt: Play A2. Any place on the fretboard counts.
Play D3. Any place on the fretboard counts.
Play G3. Any place on the fretboard counts.

steps.title: Find it twice
steps.body: Pick the open D string, then find the same note on the A string. Pluck both and listen: they sound the same.

items.prompt: Play A2. Use a different place from the open string if you can.
